name: Capture One
tagline: Catalog and adjust local raw files with a deliberately limited editing pipeline
verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Capture One, catalog and adjust local raw files with a deliberately limited editing pipeline. The hard boundary is proprietary raw rendering, tethering, color tools, camera profiles, and studio workflow, plus image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish.
coreLoopDIY: Catalog local raw files, generate previews, apply non-destructive adjustments through a deliberately limited editing pipeline, and export selected originals or rendered copies.
whatYouLose: proprietary raw rendering, tethering, color tools, camera profiles, and studio workflow
moatNotes: image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish
ongoingBurden: raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Capture One because photographers pay because image quality, catalog safety, and fast handling of huge libraries matter more than cloning sliders. The recurring cost buys raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Immich
priorArt.desc: Active open-source self-hosted photo and video management platform.

alternatives.name: darktable
alternatives.desc: Local cataloging plus a deep non-destructive RAW pipeline, masks, tether-aware workflows, and batch export; less studio polish, no bill.

facts.install: Install the Windows executable, macOS disk image, Linux package, Flatpak, or AppImage
facts.engines: A local non-generative imaging pipeline; current releases can use ONNX models for subject masking, denoising, and image upscaling without a cloud account
facts.dataFormat: Original photos stay untouched; edits, ratings, tags, and history are stored in a local SQLite library and portable XMP sidecar files, with thumbnails and cache data in the user profile
facts.gapVsPaid: Its RAW pipeline is deep, but tethered capture, Sessions, live-view studio operation, and camera-specific color workflows are less polished than Capture One's.
facts.setupBlocker: macOS may require a Gatekeeper right-click Open or xattr step; the larger obstacle is learning darktable's module-heavy workflow rather than installation

alternatives.name: digiKam
alternatives.desc: A mature local and network catalog with metadata, ratings, RAW import, batch tools, and a serviceable editor.

facts.install: Install the Windows installer/portable build, macOS package, or a Linux AppImage, Flatpak, Snap, or distribution package
facts.engines: Local OpenCV and packaged machine-learning models for face recognition, automatic tagging, image-quality scoring, similarity search, red-eye detection, and related catalog analysis
facts.dataFormat: Photos remain in selected local or network collection folders; catalog, thumbnails, faces, and similarity data live in SQLite by default or MariaDB, with metadata and ratings optionally written into files or XMP sidecars
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a capable catalog, not a professional tethered-capture and studio-session editor comparable to Capture One.
facts.setupBlocker: First-run collection and database choices are technical, and scanning a large library plus downloading recognition models can take a long time

alternatives.name: RapidRAW
alternatives.desc: A deliberately simpler catalog and RAW editor with presets, masks, ratings, culling, and batch work; young but genuinely installable.

facts.install: Install the Windows .exe, macOS .dmg, or Linux AppImage/DEB/Flatpak; Android is an experimental sideload
facts.engines: Local subject, sky, and foreground masking, NIND denoising, LaMa inpainting, and optional handoff to a user-run ComfyUI backend
facts.dataFormat: Photos are never moved; non-destructive adjustments are stored in a documented .rrdata sidecar next to each image, while thumbnails, logs, and downloaded models live in local application data
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks Capture One's professional tethering, Sessions workflow, mature camera profiles, and proven high-volume studio reliability.
facts.setupBlocker: Desktop binaries are unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper need manual bypass steps; Linux AppImage users may also need libfuse2

rejectedAlternatives.name: Immich
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Central photo backup and browsing do not replace desktop RAW adjustments, sessions, masks, or controlled exports.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Capture One Pro plan and a personal local photo catalog DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Capture One in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, Rust image libraries, SQLite, and local filesystem access; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: catalog local raw files, generate previews, apply non-destructive adjustments through a deliberately limited editing pipeline, and export selected originals or rendered copies.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Index selected folders without moving or rewriting originals and store only catalog data in SQLite.
Generate thumbnails and previews, read EXIF, detect duplicates by hash, and monitor file changes.
Provide timeline, folders, albums, ratings, flags, tags, search, and side-by-side compare.
Store edits as reversible parameters for crop, rotate, exposure, contrast, white balance, and saturation.
Render exports to a new folder with explicit color space, quality, size, and metadata choices.
Add catalog backup, missing-file repair, integrity scan, and a clear original-safety guarantee.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a proprietary raw-rendering engine.
Deliberately leave out hosted cross-device photo sync and client galleries.
Deliberately leave out frontier culling, retouching, and generative models.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
